arrays-02.title: Broadcast along the missing axis
steps: Two rows, three features per row.
Add the same three bias values to each row.
arrays-02.note: Conceptual example: broadcasting repeats values logically; it does not add a new example axis. A target (2, 1) and prediction (2,) can accidentally form a (2, 2) result.

state-01.title: A key is an explicit input
steps: Keep one owner for the sequence.
Use one child to continue, another for this sample.
state-01.note: Reusing sample_key reproduces the same random computation. Splitting does not mutate the parent key; decide which child belongs to each computation.

state-02.title: Structure travels with the leaves
steps: Names and containers describe the structure.
Apply a matching operation to each array leaf.
The optimizer and gradients must agree on the tree.
state-02.note: A pytree is a nested structure with array leaves, not one large flattened tensor. Shape and dtype still matter separately at each leaf.

state-03.title: Carry state through a compiled loop
steps: Start with an explicit state tree.
Return the next state and this step’s output.
scan collects outputs and returns the final carry.
state-03.note: Every carry leaf keeps the same shape and dtype through the loop. Outputs are stacked along the scan axis; the carry is the state that connects steps.

optimization-04.title: Optimizer history is part of training state
steps: Evaluate the objective at the current parameters.
Pass both updated values into the next step.
optimization-04.note: Optax updates are increments applied to parameters. Adam also carries moments and a count; restoring parameters alone cannot reproduce the same next update.

recovery-04.title: Restore one consistent training boundary
steps: Identify the state needed to choose and process the next batch.
Wait for the local checkpoint operation to finish.
same next batch → same next transition
Compare the restored transition with uninterrupted training.
recovery-04.note: This illustrates the lesson’s completed local snapshot boundary. It is verified separately from power-loss durability, asynchronous failure recovery or multi-host coordination.

distributed-01.title: One global array, four local row shards
steps: The program sees an eight-row array.
A four-device mesh splits the chosen axis.
Local storage and global array semantics are different views.
distributed-01.note: Conceptual layout for eight rows and four logical CPU devices. All devices share one host; this explains partitioning rather than simulating accelerator speed or network behavior.
